The gap peaked at roughly 40 percentage points in the mid-1950s, when Gallup polls showed approval of the Supreme Court's desegregation ruling far lower in the South than in the rest of the country. I'm working from memory of those polls, not a checked source, so the exact figures may be off. I'd verify them against Gallup's 1956-57 data before relying on the number.

CONFIDENCE: 40
